questions.question_text: Which of these is not equivalent to $\ln(16x^2)$?

options.why: This follows from $\ln(16x^2)=\ln16+\ln(x^2)$.
Since $2\ln(4x)=2\ln4+2\ln x=\ln16+2\ln x$.
The product rule and power rule give the same expression in reversed order.

questions.solution_text: For $x>0$, $\ln(16x^2)=\ln16+2\ln x$. Option B gives $2\ln(16x)=2\ln16+2\ln x$, which has an extra $\ln16$ and is not equivalent.

questions.question_text: If $N=At^n$, which of these plots would give a straight line graph?

options.why: A power law is generally curved on ordinary axes rather than a straight line.
Taking a logarithm of N alone does not remove the power of t from the horizontal variable.
The response N still has a power-law dependence and is not linear in $\ln t$.

questions.solution_text: Taking natural logarithms gives $\ln N=\ln A+n\ln t$. This has the straight-line form $Y=c+mX$ when $\ln N$ is plotted against $\ln t$.
